Subject: Request: Audit log exports for compliance evidence

Hi Aditya,

We're preparing for a scheduled regulatory inspection next month and need a package of audit/access logs for specific production dates (2026-08-01 to 2026-10-31). Our compliance team has asked for:
- Complete API access logs and admin action trails for the tenant (including model routing/fallback events).
- Proof that the logs were stored in US region and details of the retention window.
- A machine-readable export (CSV/NDJSON) plus an MD5 checksum for each file.

Can Redwood produce these exports, and how long will it take? Also--we need confirmation that any exported package does not include customer plaintext data beyond the metadata captured in the access logs.

Hi Sarah — thanks for the checklist and the heads up. We can produce an evidence bundle for the date range you specified. A few quick clarifying points so we scope this properly:

1) Tenant identification: please confirm the tenant/org ID you want included (or confirm account email).
2) Export scope: do you want all API request/response metadata + control-plane (admin) events, or only access/auth events?
3) Residency & keying: do you require the exports to be generated from US-based storage (we support region-scoped exports) and do you need an HSM-backed signing step?
4) Redaction: we will not include full user-provided prompt/response content by default — exports contain timestamps, request IDs, model id, route decisions, and high-level token counts. If you believe you received extra payloads we can run a targeted scrub.

Estimated timeline: once scope and tenant are confirmed, we can deliver a staged export in 3 business days for the CSV/NDJSON package (full historical run may take longer depending on volume). We'll provide MD5 checksums and a manifest.

I'm looping Grace (security engineering) to confirm retention windows and the export process.

Hi all — thanks for the details, Sarah, and thanks Aditya for the heads up. Below is a concise Q&A + runbook summary so we can set expectations with Clearview.

Q: Retention windows — what can we provide?
A: Hosted API (default tier): audit/access logs are retained for 90 days in hot storage, with a rolling cold archive available up to 2 years depending on plan. Dedicated: retention configurable per contract (we've seen 1–7 years in enterprise agreements). Private: retention is governed by the customer's on-prem/VPC policies. We can confirm Clearview's current plan allows for 2-year archive retrieval; I'll validate the contract.

Q: Export formats & content scope?
A: Exports are offered as NDJSON (recommended) and CSV (tabular subset). Each record includes timestamp, request_id, tenant_id, api_path, status_code, model_variant, routing_decision, latency_ms, user_agent, and admin_action metadata. We explicitly exclude raw user prompt/response bodies from the default export. If Clearview requires additional fields (e.g., full payload), we need a signed contractual addendum and a privacy impact review.

Q: Residency & signing
A: We support region-scoped export jobs. For US-resident exports we will spawn the job from US storage endpoints and sign the bundle with the customer's KMS key if requested (HSM option available under enterprise). The signed bundle includes per-file MD5 and a manifest.

Q: Generation timeline & size limits
A: Typical delivery: small tenants (<200GB) — 1–3 business days. Large volumes (multi-TB) require 5–10 business days and may be split into multi-part archives. There is a per-job throughput cap (we throttle exports to protect serving performance); we will coordinate a maintenance window for large pulls.

Q: Deletion & proof
A: On-demand deletion of stored audit ranges is allowed for Dedicated/Private customers per contract; for Hosted API we can remove archived copies and provide a signed deletion certificate. Deletion workflow: open a support ticket (reference SUP-7891), provide tenant and timestamp ranges, perform secure wipe from archives, and post a signed manifest stating file checksums removed and timestamps of the operation. Note: deletion does not alter already-exported bundles you retain.

Runbook (high-level):
1) Validate tenant/org ID and file ranges with customer.
2) Create export job via admin console: Console > Security > Audit Exports > New job (select NDJSON/CSV, date range, residency).
3) System generates staged archive in region-scoped storage; security engineering can opt to sign with customer KMS.
4) QA: sanity-check record counts, run MD5 on parts, produce manifest.
5) Deliver via secure transfer (pre-signed URL to customer S3 or password-protected transfer).
6) If deletion requested, open deletion SOP workflow and produce signed deletion certificate.

Attachments: export_playbook.md (detailed internal steps), SOP_export_command_samples.txt (CLI examples). I'll attach both to the support case.

Action items for Aditya: please confirm tenant ID and whether Clearview wants HSM signing. Sarah — once you confirm, I'll open SUP-7891 and scope the job.

Regards,
Grace O'Connor
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
